references.text: Reuel is mentioned as another name for Jethro, who was Moses' father-in-law and a Midianite.
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, is introduced as the priest of Midian.
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, the Midianite, visits Moses and hears about the Lord's deeds for Israel.
The continuation of the conversation between Moses and Hobab, where Moses asks him to join as a guide.
The Kenites, descendants of Moses' father-in-law, went up from the City of Palms together with the tribe of Judah.
Heber the Kenite had separated himself from Hobab the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law.
God's promise to Abraham to give the land to his descendants, which Moses refers to.
The Lord speaks about the promise to give Israel a good land.
God's promise to give the land to Israel, which Moses refers to in his speech to Hobab.
